title: a/an and the
subtitle: a window / the window
summary: Use a/an when there are many things like it, and the when it is clear which thing or person you mean.

lesson.heading: a window or the window?
lesson.text: A room has three windows. Somebody is hot and says: *Can you open **a** window?* Any of the three is fine. In another room there is only one window. Here we say: *Can you open **the** window?* Everybody knows which window.

examples.text: I've got **a** car. (there are many cars and I've got one)
I'm going to clean **the** car tomorrow. (= my car)

lesson.heading: a/an and the

right.label: the - we know which one
examples: We enjoyed our holiday. **The hotel** was very nice.
Lisa is **the youngest student** in her class.

lesson.note: There is only one capital of France and only one youngest student in the class, so we use **the**.

lesson.heading: First a, then the
lesson.text: When you talk about something for the first time, use **a/an**. After that the other person knows which thing you mean, so use **the**.

examples.text: I bought **a** jacket and **a** shirt. **The** jacket was cheap, but **the** shirt was expensive.

lesson.heading: the ... because there is only one
lesson.note: A room has one door and one floor, a town has one station, so we say **the**.

lesson.heading: the in everyday sentences
lesson.text: We say **the** when it is clear which thing or person we mean. Often it is the one in this room, this house, this town or this shop.

examples.text: *A:* Where's Tom? *B:* In **the kitchen**. (= the kitchen of this house)
Turn off **the light** and close **the door**.
Do you live far from **the centre**? (= the centre of your town)
I'd like to speak to **the manager**, please.

lesson.text: Ask yourself: does the other person know which one I mean? Yes -> **the**. No -> **a/an**.

exercises.prompt: You look very tired. You need ___ holiday.
exercises.explanation: Any holiday - not one special holiday - so we use a.

exercises.prompt: Eve is ___ interesting person. You should meet her.
exercises.explanation: There are many interesting people and Eve is one. interesting starts with a vowel sound, so an.
The house has one garden and we both know it, so the garden.
There is only one capital of France, so we say the capital.

exercises.prompt: I bought a jacket and a shirt. ___ jacket was cheap, but the shirt was expensive.
exercises.explanation: Now you know which jacket I mean - the one I bought.

exercises.prompt: Somebody is speaking. Match each sentence with the words that complete it.

pairs.left: Can I have ... of coffee, please?

exercises.prompt: It's ___ nice morning. Let's go for a walk.
exercises.explanation: There are many nice mornings and today is one of them.
Canada is a very big country. English needs a before a singular noun here.

exercises.statement: I like this room, but I don't like colour of carpet.
exercises.explanation: I like this room, but I don't like the colour of the carpet. There is one carpet in this room and it has one colour.
We say a headache, like a cold and a temperature.

exercises.prompt: Which word goes in the gap: a/an or the?

items.text: Shall we go out for ___ meal this evening?
What is ___ name of this village?
What is ___ largest city in Canada?
Can you tell me how to get to ___ city centre?
We live in an old house near ___ station.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.
exercises.answer: We live in an old house near the station.
exercises.explanation: an old house = one of many houses; the station = the one station in this town.
